model_output.verdict: A construction project manager with project values, trade counts and delivery results a recruiter can use.
write_up: You manage concurrent tenant-improvement projects and have delivered a grocery store build. A recruiter can see the project values, the number of trades and where you beat schedule. The main question is how you kept change orders down.

The grocery store line is the model: it names the build, its value and when you delivered it against schedule. Your earlier scheduling work is specific, too, and Experience is where it belongs, above Education.

cards.line: - Delivered a $14M grocery store build 3 weeks ahead of schedule in 2024
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this. It ties a concrete project to a delivery result without making the reader hunt for context.

cards.line: - Kept change orders under 3% of contract value across 2024 and 2025 projects
cards.cannot_tell: The result is strong, but a recruiter can't see what you did to keep change orders down. Your approach would show how you managed that part of the work.
cards.example: Kept change orders under 3% of contract value across 2024 and 2025 projects by [approach]
cards.question: What did you do to keep change orders under 3% of contract value across those projects?

fit.note: Your experience points toward construction project management in tenant improvements and retail builds. The current role shows both concurrent project management and a completed grocery store build.
